docs.agreement.p1: The first time Flipcopy opens it shows its licence agreement. Read it to the end and Agree becomes available. Until you agree, Flipcopy reads nothing, copies nothing and adds nothing to your track's audio.
docs.agreement.p2: Your answer is kept on your computer and shared by every open copy of Flipcopy, in every DAW and in the standalone app. If you decline, choose Read it again whenever you are ready.
docs.agreement.title: The licence agreement
docs.browser.p1: The browser opens on its Categories: Copies, every page and mix you have made, and Recent, the originals you last put on the glass. Under them are the folders you have added; choose + Add Folder to add one, up to 128. A folder on a drive that is not plugged in keeps its place and says it isn’t connected right now. To stop browsing a folder, right-click it, or select it and press Delete; nothing on disk is touched.
docs.browser.p2: Open a folder to walk it as a tree. Type to filter it by name, pick a tag or Starred to narrow it, and choose Show all files to see the sidecar files Flipcopy hides, such as .asd and .reapeaks. Back and Forward take you through the places you have been.
docs.browser.p3: Walk the rows with ↑ and ↓: each row you land on plays once in the preview. → opens a folder and ← closes it. Enter puts the selected file on the glass, and so does dragging its row onto the copier.
docs.browser.p4: The first time you add a folder, Flipcopy counts its files, with a bar that shows how far it has got. It reads at most 12 folders deep and 50,000 files, and never follows a shortcut out of the folder.
docs.browser.title: The browser
docs.copier.p1: Put an audio or MIDI file on the glass: drop it from Explorer or Finder anywhere on the window, drag it from the browser or the preview strip onto the copier, press Enter on a row in the browser, or press Enter on the empty glass to choose one. The copier prints the original and lays it face-down on the glass. Putting a file on the glass never starts a copy.
docs.copier.p2: Press the green START key, or Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on a Mac). The lid closes, the lamp sweeps, and the copy slides out onto the tray: an audio loop comes out as MIDI, one page for each part the copier hears; a MIDI file comes out as audio, one page for each part. Esc or the red STOP key cancels it; the grey HOME key clears the glass.
docs.copier.p3: Every page is a real file in Documents/Freally Flipcopy/Copies, numbered, and never moved, overwritten or deleted. Grab a page by the lime frame round its printed clip and drag it straight onto a track in your DAW, or drag the whole stack at once.
docs.copier.p4: The copier’s sounds play through the plugin’s own output, quietly, never while your DAW plays and never into a bounce. Turn them off or down in Settings.
docs.copier.title: Making a copy
docs.intro: This manual grows with every version. Right now it covers what version 0.4.0 does; the full illustrated manual, with a screenshot for every step, arrives with the beta.
docs.language.p1: Flipcopy speaks eighteen languages. It starts in your system's language; to choose another, open Settings with the gear at the top of the browser and pick one. The choice applies to every copy of Flipcopy on the computer.
docs.language.title: Languages
docs.preview.p1: The preview player sits under the browser. An audio file shows its real waveform. A MIDI file shows its notes and plays through Preview Piano, the same sound a copy uses unless you choose another, so you hear what the copy will sound like.
docs.preview.p2: Space plays and pauses, Stop goes back to the start, and a click or a drag on the strip moves the playhead. Loop repeats the file, Play when selected (the headphones) plays each file you select, and the slider sets the level. The preview plays through Flipcopy’s own output and never into a bounce. A WAV file of any length plays; a file in another format plays if it is five minutes or shorter.
docs.preview.p3: Click the original on the glass, or a page on the tray, to hear it. When a copy is finished, Copy plays all its pages together and Original plays the file on the glass, from the same place in the music, so you can hear the difference before you drag. Playing it is never required: the pages can be dragged as soon as the last one lands.
docs.preview.p4: The strip wears the same lime frame as a page. Drag it onto the glass to put that file there.
docs.preview.title: The preview player
docs.privacy.p1: Flipcopy has no account and no telemetry, and the plugin and standalone app contain no networking code at all. Your files and your copies never leave your computer.
docs.privacy.p2: It contains no AI of any kind: every copy is made by classic, deterministic signal processing, and a build gate fails if a machine-learning library is ever added.
docs.privacy.title: Privacy and the network
docs.report.p1: If Flipcopy itself fails, such as a copy it could not write, the screen offers Report. It opens a page in your web browser that shows exactly what the report holds; nothing is sent unless you press Send there. A file the copier refuses, because it is too long, silent or not audio, is not a failure, and the screen says why instead.
docs.report.title: When something goes wrong
docs.start.p1: Flipcopy runs inside your DAW as a CLAP, VST3 or AU plugin, or on its own as a standalone app. Put it on any audio track: it passes the track's audio through exactly as it arrives, so it is safe to leave in place.
docs.start.p2: There are no downloads before version 1.0.0, and the source code is private.
docs.start.title: Getting started
docs.window.p1: On one side is the browser, with the preview player docked under it. The rest of the window is the stage, where the copier stands. Drag the line between them to make the browser wider or narrower, or focus it and use the arrow keys.
docs.window.p2: Press Ctrl+B (Cmd+B on a Mac), or the button at the browser’s edge, to fold the browser and its preview away: the stage takes the whole window. Press it again and they come back at the width you left them. Flipcopy remembers which you chose.
docs.window.title: The window
features.audioToMidi.body: The drums, bass, melody, countermelody and chords found in a loop, one page each, printed back to back from a single scan, so they drag into your DAW as separate tracks.
features.audioToMidi.title: Audio → MIDI
features.browser.body: A file browser with a preview player, from Freally Oscillate. It shows a waveform for audio and the notes for MIDI, and plays MIDI through the instrument the copy uses.
features.browser.title: The browser
features.copier.body: A photoreal copy machine rendered in Blender. Put a clip on the glass and it prints the real thing: every note, or the real waveform, with its tempo, length and levels.
features.copier.title: The copier
features.daw.body: CLAP, VST3 and AU, plus a standalone app for working without a DAW and for Pro Tools. Windows, macOS and Linux.
features.daw.title: In any DAW
features.drag.body: Every page wears a lime-green frame around its clip. Grab it and drop it on a track. The file is real, and Flipcopy never overwrites or deletes it.
features.drag.title: Drag the copy
features.free.body: No tier, no account, no telemetry, no network, no model. Classic signal processing, enforced by a build gate rather than promised.
features.free.title: Free, offline, no AI
features.midiToAudio.body: A MIDI file played through a real instrument, and drums through a drum machine, printed as an audio file you can drag.
features.midiToAudio.title: MIDI → audio
features.start.body: Dropping a clip only places it on the glass. Nothing is copied until you press START, so nothing happens that you did not ask for.
features.start.title: The green START
features.title: What is in it
featuresPage.cards.audioToMidi.body: A loop comes out as the parts in it — drums on their own lanes, bass, melody, a countermelody where there is one, and the chord progression — one page and one MIDI file each, from a single scan. A part that is not there gets no page. Or copy a sung line on its own.
featuresPage.cards.audioToMidi.title: Audio → MIDI, in parts
featuresPage.cards.browser.body: A file browser from Freally Oscillate: up to 128 folders, back and forward, tags, stars and a keyboard walk. The preview shows the real waveform or the notes, plays MIDI through the same sound the copy uses, and plays a finished stack in sync, with an A/B against the original.
featuresPage.cards.browser.title: The browser and the Preview Player
featuresPage.cards.copier.body: A photoreal copy machine rendered in Blender, with its own sounds. Put a clip on the glass and it prints the real thing — the waveform, or every note — with its data: tempo, length, notes or levels.
featuresPage.cards.copier.title: The copier
featuresPage.cards.copies.body: Every copy is a real, verified file in your Copies folder — numbered, and never moved, overwritten or deleted, so a project that uses it never loses it. Page back through every copy you have made, save one again, show it in its folder, or put it back on the glass.
featuresPage.cards.copies.title: Copies are forever
featuresPage.cards.daw.body: CLAP and VST3 on Windows, macOS and Linux, AU on macOS, and a standalone app for working without a DAW — and for Pro Tools, by dragging. Saved with your project, safe in many instances at once, and able to scan straight from a track.
featuresPage.cards.daw.title: In every DAW
featuresPage.cards.drag.body: Every page wears a lime-green frame: grab it and drop the file on a track. Or drag the whole stack — All parts lands as one track per part, Complete mix as one clip. Each file is named the way your DAW should show it, such as Loop - Bassline - 120 BPM - C# Minor.
featuresPage.cards.drag.title: Drag the copy
featuresPage.cards.midiToAudio.body: A MIDI file played through any of the 1,648 instruments Freally MIDI Master uses — a sound for each part and a drum machine for the drums — and printed as one audio page per part, plus the whole mix. WAV, AIFF, FLAC or MP3, at the sample rate and bit depth you choose.
featuresPage.cards.midiToAudio.title: MIDI → audio, through real instruments
featuresPage.cards.offline.body: No telemetry and no model. Every copy is made by classic signal processing, and the plugin and the app never go online. The one exception is an update check that stays off unless you switch it on, run by a separate program.
featuresPage.cards.offline.title: Offline, private, no AI
featuresPage.cards.settings.body: The copier's own screen holds the copy settings: which parts, the grid and swing, the tempo and where it comes from, the sound for each part, the file format and the tail. A build gate checks that each setting really changes the copy.
featuresPage.cards.settings.title: Settings on the touch screen
featuresPage.cards.skins.body: Five skins, each a raised chassis rendered in Blender and shared by every Freally app, in light and dark, beside plain light and dark modes. The copier is rendered again for each one, so it always stands on its own ground.
featuresPage.cards.skins.title: Skins, light and dark
featuresPage.cards.start.body: Dropping a clip only places it on the glass. Nothing is copied until you press START; STOP cancels a scan and HOME clears the glass, so nothing happens that you did not ask for.
featuresPage.cards.start.title: Only the green START copies
featuresPage.cards.studio.body: Open any copy in a piano roll, one tab per part, edited exactly as in Freally MIDI Master. Hear it through any instrument, shape it on a mixer with realistic knobs, play it through your own drum kit or one of your samples, and send the edit back to the glass to print as a new copy.
featuresPage.cards.studio.title: The Studio
featuresPage.cards.title: What version 1.0 does
featuresPage.coming.downloads: There are no downloads before version 1.0, and none on this page.
featuresPage.coming.intro: Stated plainly, because a feature list that hides its gaps is not worth reading. This page is version 1.0, and Flipcopy is built one rung at a time: not everything on it is built yet. Each rung on the road to 1.0 is marked with its state.
featuresPage.coming.title: What is still coming
featuresPage.compare.asOf: Flipcopy's column is version 1.0, which is not out yet, and its price is today's: Flipcopy is free today, and future versions may be sold. The other products change too; this table is as of 1 October 2026.
featuresPage.compare.intro: Freally Flipcopy 1.0 next to the commercial tools producers use to turn audio into MIDI and MIDI into audio. Every cell for another product comes from its maker's own pages, checked on 1 October 2026, and prices are US list prices as of October 2026.
featuresPage.compare.note.byHand: stems first, then each by hand
featuresPage.compare.note.link: sends audio to its own app
featuresPage.compare.note.playbackOnly: plays it, but exports no audio
featuresPage.compare.row.drag: Drag the result straight onto a DAW track
featuresPage.compare.row.midiToAudio: Turns MIDI into audio through built-in instruments
featuresPage.compare.row.parts: One loop split into its parts, each its own MIDI file
featuresPage.compare.row.plugin: Works inside a DAW as a plugin
featuresPage.compare.summary: The short version: only Flipcopy has all of it — both directions, the parts, the drag, the plugin, all three systems and no AI.
featuresPage.compare.theyWin: Where they win: Melodyne Studio, RipX, AnthemScore and Ableton Live can write out the individual notes of a chord from a polyphonic recording (Melodyne only from an instrument recorded on its own); Flipcopy gives you the progression instead, and says so. RipX, Ableton Live Suite and Logic Pro also separate a mix into audio stems, which Flipcopy 1.0 does not.
featuresPage.compare.title: Side by side with the commercial tools
featuresPage.free.body: Everything Flipcopy does today is free, for everyone: no paid tier, no subscription, no account and no trial that runs out. The copies you make are yours, as far as the files you copied were yours to use.
featuresPage.free.title: Free today
featuresPage.lead: A copy machine for your clips. Audio in, MIDI out, split into its parts; MIDI in, audio out, through real instruments — and every copy drags straight into your DAW.
featuresPage.limits.aax: It is not a Pro Tools plugin: in Pro Tools, use the standalone app and drag the copy onto the timeline.
featuresPage.limits.chords: It does not write out every note of a chord heard in a mixed recording: chords come back as the progression, and the page says so.
featuresPage.limits.loops: It copies loops, not whole songs: the glass takes clips of up to 16 bars, and refuses a longer one with its length.
featuresPage.limits.stems: It does not separate a mixed recording into audio stems: a loop's parts come out as MIDI.
featuresPage.limits.title: What 1.0 does not do
featuresPage.numbers.bars: bars: the longest loop the glass takes
featuresPage.numbers.directions: directions: audio → MIDI and MIDI → audio
featuresPage.numbers.formats: file formats it writes: MIDI, WAV, AIFF, FLAC and MP3
featuresPage.numbers.instruments: instruments to play a MIDI copy through
featuresPage.numbers.parts: kinds of part it copies: drums, bass, melody, countermelody, chords and a sung line
featuresPage.numbers.plugins: plugin formats, plus a standalone app
featuresPage.numbers.systems: operating systems: Windows, macOS and Linux
featuresPage.version: This page describes Freally Flipcopy version 1.0: everything on it is in 1.0, and nothing planned for after 1.0 is on it.
featuresPage.why.dsp.body: Onsets, pitch tracking, chroma and a deterministic renderer, with no model anywhere. The same file, the same settings and the same version give the same copy, byte for byte, every time.
featuresPage.why.dsp.title: Classic signal processing
featuresPage.why.honest.body: No blank pages and no guesses dressed up as a transcription. Chords say they are a progression, a clip too long for the glass is refused with its length rather than cut, and a sung line left alone says so.
featuresPage.why.honest.title: Honest copies
featuresPage.why.local.body: No telemetry and no cloud. Your files and your copies never leave your computer, and a build gate fails if networking code is ever added to the plugin or the app.
featuresPage.why.local.title: It stays on your machine
featuresPage.why.mix.body: The copier's sounds and the preview play quietly through the plugin, and never into a bounce. While they are silent, your track's audio passes through untouched.
featuresPage.why.mix.title: Nothing reaches your mix by accident
featuresPage.why.print.body: Every page is drawn from the bytes of the file it drags. The notes, tempo and length on the paper are the notes, tempo and length that land on your track.
featuresPage.why.print.title: What you see is what you drag
featuresPage.why.tempo.body: The plugin reads your project's tempo and never changes it, and every tempo Flipcopy prints names where it came from: the loop, the file, its name, your DAW, or you.
featuresPage.why.tempo.title: It follows your DAW
featuresPage.why.title: Why it is built the way it is

honest.chords.body: A chord part is printed as the progression it follows, not the exact voicing that was played, and the page says so in so many words.
honest.chords.title: Chords come back as a progression
honest.downloads.body: No beta on this page, no preview build, no early access. A copier that half-works is worse than one that is not there yet.
honest.downloads.title: There are no downloads before 1.0.0
honest.network.body: The plugin and the standalone app contain no networking code at all, and a build gate fails if any is added. A later version may add an update check that is off unless you switch it on, run by a separate program.
honest.network.title: It never goes online
honest.title: The things most sites put at the bottom
honest.transcription.body: Finding notes in a finished mix is hard, and Flipcopy does it with classic signal processing rather than a model. It will miss some notes and hear some that are not there. It prints what it found, and says what it could not do.
honest.transcription.title: A MIDI copy of a mix is a transcription
ladder.intro: One line per version. This is the same ladder the private plan follows — if one moves, both move, and a build gate compares them.
ladder.note: A version that is done is built and tagged. It is not a download: there are none, and there will not be until 1.0.0.
ladder.rung.v0.1.0: The foundation: the plugin loads as CLAP, VST3 and AU and as a standalone app, passes your audio through untouched, asks you to accept its licence, and every quality gate runs.
ladder.rung.v0.2.0: The copier and the first copy: the machine in the window, the green START, and a MIDI file copied into audio you drag straight into your DAW.
ladder.rung.v0.3.0: Audio to MIDI: drop a loop on the glass, press START, and drag out its drums, bass, melody and chords as MIDI.
ladder.rung.v0.4.0: The file browser and preview player: find a sample or a MIDI clip, hear it, see it, and drag it onto the glass. Everything essential is here.
ladder.rung.v0.5.0: The touch screen: copy settings, instruments for your copies, file formats, and the history of every copy you have made.
ladder.rung.v0.5.5: The Studio: open any copy in a piano roll, change its notes, hear it through any instrument, and print your edit as a new copy.
ladder.rung.v0.5.7: The mixer and your own instruments: realistic knobs to shape every part, your own drum kits and samples, favourites, and one instrument library shared by every Freally app.
ladder.rung.v0.5.9: Skins and light mode: five skins, each a raised chassis rendered in Blender and the same across every Freally app, in light and dark, beside a new light mode.
ladder.rung.v0.6.0: In every DAW: saved with your project, several copies at once, scanning straight from a track, and checked DAW by DAW.
ladder.rung.v0.7.0: The standalone app at full strength, macOS and Linux, and the video of the copier at work.
ladder.rung.v0.8.0: Accuracy, realism and speed: better transcriptions, a more convincing machine, and every performance budget enforced.
ladder.rung.v1.0.0: The release — and the first downloads this site has ever offered.
ladder.rung.v1.0.0-beta: Hardened: installers for three systems, the optional update check, and the full illustrated manual. Still no downloads on this site.
ladder.rung.v1.0.0-rc: The release candidate: every file reviewed and every host tested by hand.
ladder.rung.v1.1.0: The document feeder: copy a whole folder in one go.
ladder.rung.v1.3.0: Score copies: MusicXML and a staff-notation print.
ladder.rung.v1.4.0: Bridges to the other Freally products.
ladder.rung.v1.5.0: Pro Tools as a plugin (AAX), if Avid's terms allow it for a free product.
ladder.rung.v1.6.0: Groove copies, and rough, AI-free stem copies.
ladder.title: The road to 1.0

site.tagline: Put it on the glass. Press START. Drag the copy.
what.p1: Turning a loop into MIDI, or a MIDI file into audio, usually means a chain of tools, an export, a re-import and a lot of guessing about what came out.
what.p2: Flipcopy is a copy machine. Put an audio file or a MIDI file on its glass and it prints the original — the real waveform, or every note, with its data. Press the green START and it prints the copy in the other form: audio in, MIDI out; MIDI in, audio out.
what.p3: The copy comes out as a printed page with a lime-green frame around its clip. Grab the frame and drag it onto a track in your DAW. Every copy is a real file that stays where it is, so your project never loses it.
what.title: What it is
